description: A company commander must approve the next day's motor-pool maintenance board for three support vehicles, setting the active work sequence, disposition, release timing, and coordination actions needed before the vehicles are returned to service.

shared_context.S1: The motor pool has one maintenance bay available tomorrow for the three vehicles listed on the draft board: M-12, V-8, and G-3.
shared_context.S2: Capt. Alvarez signs the final maintenance sequence and release instructions.
shared_context.S3: The draft board lists all three vehicles for routine service, with no special sequencing or parts action recorded.
shared_context.S4: At the routine maintenance-board check-in before the commander signs, the maintenance chief, dispatcher, and supply NCO report any changes from their sections.

PF1.text: During this morning's inspection, SFC Morgan confirmed that M-12 failed its brake-line integrity check and must be held for brake repair before any return-to-service inspection; the result is in the maintenance worksheet but has not yet been entered on the draft board.

PF2.text: Sgt. Patel confirmed that V-8 is assigned to a scheduled water resupply run tomorrow evening and must be released from the bay by exactly 1600 to complete dispatch preparation; the tasking is on the dispatcher's board but has not yet been reflected in the maintenance sequence.

PF3.text: Sgt. Lewis confirmed that G-3's replacement alternator is on the 1400 supply truck and must be received before G-3's electrical service is started; the shipment confirmation arrived after the draft board was printed and has not yet been posted to the work order.

acceptance_conditions: The active maintenance sequence must place V-8 before G-3; M-12 may be omitted from the active sequence or listed separately before or after them because it is handled as a brake-repair hold outside routine service.
M-12 must be held for brake repair.
V-8 must be released by exactly 1600.
G-3's alternator must be received at 1400 before electrical service begins.
The board must include coordination actions mentioning V-8's 1600 release deadline or dispatch preparation and the G-3 alternator receipt dependency.
The commander must cite the confirmed M-12 brake-line failure as a justification.

content_checks.C4: 'alternator' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] and 'service' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] and ('before' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] or 'until' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'] or 'after' in decisions['G-3_parts_action'])
content_checks.C6: any('V-8' in c['detail'] and ('1600' in c['detail'] or 'dispatch preparation' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) and any('G-3' in c['detail'] and 'alternator' in c['detail'] and (('1400' in c['detail'] and 'receipt' in c['detail']) or 'before' in c['detail'] or 'until' in c['detail'] or 'after' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed brake-line failure changes M-12 from routine service to a brake-repair hold, so the disposition must specify brake repair and cite PF1.

The water-resupply task requires V-8 to appear before G-3 in the active sequence, fixes V-8's release deadline at exactly 1600, and requires a commitment mentioning that deadline or dispatch preparation.

The confirmed 1400 alternator delivery requires G-3 to follow V-8 in the active sequence, requires alternator receipt before electrical service, and requires a commitment addressing the alternator receipt dependency.
